proof:
Source. Step 7 of the supplied proof of chart_pieces. That is Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 68–73): 'just define the M_j inductively by M_0 = M ∩ N_0 and M_j = M ∩ N_j ∖ ⋃_{i<j} M_i … the sets M_j so constructed are all Hⁿ-measurable if M is'. The construction is applied to the image sets and then pulled back to the parameter sets.

1. (Borel images.) A_j := ψ_j(Y_j) is Borel. ℝ^N is Polish, Y_j is Borel, and ψ_j is continuous and injective on Y_j, so the Lusin–Souslin theorem applies (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).

2. (First-hit sets.) D_j := A_j ∖ ⋃_{i<j} A_i is Borel: a Borel set minus a finite union of Borel sets.

3. (Parameter pieces.) Y'_j := Y_j ∩ ψ_j⁻¹(D_j) ⊆ Y_j. It is Borel, because ψ_j is continuous, hence Borel measurable.

4. (Images.) For any map ψ and sets S, T, ψ(S ∩ ψ⁻¹(T)) = ψ(S) ∩ T. Hence ψ_j(Y'_j) = A_j ∩ D_j = D_j, since D_j ⊆ A_j.

5. (Disjointness.) Let i ≠ j, say i < j. Every x ∈ D_j satisfies x ∉ A_i, while D_i ⊆ A_i; so D_i ∩ D_j = ∅. The case i > j is symmetric. By step 4, ψ_i(Y'_i) and ψ_j(Y'_j) are disjoint.

6. (Same union.)
- ⋃_j D_j ⊆ ⋃_j A_j, since D_j ⊆ A_j.
- Conversely, let x ∈ ⋃_j A_j and let j be the least index with x ∈ A_j. Then x ∉ A_i for all i < j, so x ∈ D_j.
Hence, by step 4, ⋃_j ψ_j(Y'_j) = ⋃_j D_j = ⋃_j A_j = ⋃_j ψ_j(Y_j). ∎
key_steps: A_j = ψ_j(Y_j) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin (continuous and injective on a Borel subset of a Polish space).
D_j := A_j ∖ ⋃_{i<j} A_i are Borel, pairwise disjoint, with the same union as the A_j (least index).
Y'_j := Y_j ∩ ψ_j⁻¹(D_j) is Borel and ψ_j(Y'_j) = D_j.
